openrouter_route_evidence.suggested_method_sentence: We accessed both deployments through OpenRouter, restricted each request to its declared provider, and disabled provider fallback.

actual_record_inspection.scope: Every request and response JSON directly inside the 32 final episode directories, including retained transport attempts there. Phase snapshots are not recounted; this is an audit of files, not a new call-count/cost study.

source_anchors.role: Main campaign imports the shared request client and run_episode implementation.
Each episode stores the intended model/provider pair.
The episode row is passed directly to run_episode.
Actual main payload builder pins provider.only and sets allow_fallbacks=False; finalization removes tools without changing routing.
Exploration uses row model/provider in make_payload.
Reserved final stage uses the same row model/provider.
Client serializes and saves the same payload submitted to the OpenRouter chat completions endpoint.
The A provider slug is primeintellect/bf16; MODEL is imported from model_pilot.
The imported A model identifier is google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it.

limits: Pinning provider routing does not attest a model checkpoint revision, immutable hosted weights, exact hardware or all runtime implementation details.
The provider/precision confounding remains; do not recast the two deployments as a causal model-size or precision comparison.

The older model_pilot.py also contains a price-sorted payload from a different development pilot. The main campaign imports only its MODEL and helper definitions through agent_runner_v2, and actually constructs requests using run_reader_repairs.make_payload. The 771 observed main request files resolve that potential ambiguity.
Logged responses name only PrimeIntellect and CoreWeave, consistent with the declared routes; no claim is made about unobservable provider-internal routing.
